Two sequences are similarly sorted when both run in the same monotone direction, and oppositely sorted when one increases while the other decreases.

items.text: The two finite sequences have the same length and must be ordered before the displayed forms are used.
No positivity assumption is needed for the standard real rearrangement or Chebyshev sum inequalities; the ordering assumptions do the work.
Repeated values can create several maximizing or minimizing permutations. With both sequences strictly increasing, the extremal pairings are unique.
